diagnostic_evidence.quote:
To simplify the presentation, we will limit ourselves to the case
$\alpha\left(t\right)=\beta\left(t\right)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract states convergence is proved for the coupled variable-order MHD system, whose orders alpha(t) and beta(t) are introduced as independent functions. The convergence theorem (thm:convergence) restricts to alpha(t)=beta(t), as stated in the theorem hypothesis and in the text immediately before it. The abstract and contribution (3) both omit this restriction, claiming convergence for the general two-order system.

failure_location.quote: Convergence is proved by showing that the kernels generated by the variable-order L1 approximation satisfy the assumptions of an abstract discrete fractional Gr\"{o}nwall theorem, which is then applied to the coupled MHD system.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the restriction alpha(t)=beta(t) to the abstract and contribution (3), or extend the convergence proof to the case alpha(t)≠beta(t) by tracking two separate kernel sequences through the discrete Gronwall argument.
issues.overall_effect: The scope of the convergence guarantee is overstated: convergence is established only when the momentum and magnetic orders coincide, not for the general independent-order model that is the paper's headline setting.
issues.title: Abstract and introduction overclaim convergence for independent variable orders
issues.why_classification: A short textual correction in the abstract and introduction preserves every formal result and guarantee. Extending the proof to alpha≠beta is additional work but not required to fix the overclaim.

issues.failure_explanation: The left-hand side pairs the increments phi^k − phi^{k−1} with phi^n, while the right-hand side is the L1-type fractional difference of the scalar sequence ‖phi^k‖^2. Subtracting the two sides shows the inequality is equivalent to positive semidefiniteness of the Green-type matrix {b_{n,min(i,j)}}_i,j, which follows from the strict monotonicity of the weights b_{n,k} (Lemma lem:prop_b) but is a nontrivial linear-algebraic fact. Cauchy and Young applied term-by-term give a strictly weaker lower bound involving cross terms ∑_{k<j}(d_k,d_j) that do not cancel, so the claimed proof method does not establish the result.

failure_location.quote: This inequality immediately follows from the definition in \eqref{eq:discrete_caputo}, the Cauchy inequality, and Young's inequality.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the one-line proof with a short argument showing positive semidefiniteness of the Green-type matrix {b_{n,min(i,j)}}, for example via its Cholesky/LDL^T factorisation whose pivots are b_{n,1}, b_{n,2}−b_{n,1}, …, b_{n,n}−b_{n,n−1}, all positive by Lemma lem:prop_b. This preserves every claim.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence proof invokes Lemma lem:frac1 to bound the discrete fractional time-derivative terms by (1/2)Δ_τ E_n. Without a valid proof of lem:frac1, the convergence estimate (thm:convergence) has a gap in its proof chain.
issues.title: Chain-rule-type discrete inequality has an inadequate proof
issues.why_classification: The stated inequality is true and can be proved by a contained nontrivial argument (positive semidefiniteness of a Green-type matrix), but the claimed proof method (Cauchy and Young alone) cannot establish it and must be replaced. All substantive claims survive the repair.

issues.failure_explanation: The corrected energy functional E = Θ − R subtracts a nonnegative correction R built from positive parts of δ_{j,k} = b_{j,k+1} − b_{j−1,k}. For constant orders δ_{j,k} = 0 so E = Θ ≥ 0 and the bound E + (dissipation) ≤ C(data) controls the solution via Θ ≥ (1/2)b_{n,n}‖φ^n‖^2. For variable orders δ_{j,k} can be strictly positive. The coefficient of ‖φ^k‖^2 in E is (1/2)[b_{n,k} − Σ_{j>k}(δ_{j,k})_+], which becomes negative for concrete parameter choices (e.g., two time levels with ν(t_1)=0.9, ν(t_2)=0.5, τ=0.5 give a negative coefficient for ‖φ^1‖^2). When E < 0 the displayed inequality is satisfied trivially for the E part and does not bound the discrete solution by the data, so the Stability label overstates the conclusion.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either add an explicit positivity condition on the L1 weights (e.g., b_{n,k} ≥ Σ_{j>k}(δ_{j,k})_+ for all k) as an additional hypothesis and state the resulting solution bound in terms of the corrected functional, or weaken the theorem's title and abstract claim to report only the weighted-energy inequality without asserting Stability. Alternatively, construct a modified energy functional that is nonnegative for variable orders and derive the stability bound from it.
issues.overall_effect: In the variable-order regime with sufficiently large time steps or rapidly varying orders, the stability theorem's bound does not deliver the expected bounded-solution guarantee. The stability claim for general variable-order solutions is not established by the displayed inequality alone.
issues.title: Stability bound does not control the solution when the corrected energy functional is negative
issues.why_classification: A repair requires either a new positivity hypothesis on the coefficients or a different energy construction (a contained nontrivial step), plus a restatement of the conclusion. The existing inequality remains valid and the convergence theorem (which gives the main rate) is independent, so no major loss occurs.

issues.failure_explanation: The Stokes projector is defined without a viscosity weight: (∇ψ_u, ∇v_h) = (ψ_p, ∇·v_h). In the error equation for the momentum part, the projection-error terms from diffusion and pressure combine to give (1/Re)(∇ψ_u, ∇ξ_u) − (ψ_p, ∇·ξ_u) = (1/Re − 1)(ψ_p, ∇·ξ_u), which is nonzero whenever Re ≠ 1. The displayed error equation (eq:conv_step2) shows only (1/Re)‖∇ξ_u‖^2 with no corresponding cross term, so the derivation to (1/2)Δ_τ E_n + c_0 D_n ≤ C_1 E_n + R is incomplete as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing cross term (1/Re−1)(ψ_p, ∇·ξ_u) to the error equation and absorb it via Young's inequality as ε/Re·‖∇ξ_u‖^2 + C_ε‖∇ψ_u‖^2; alternatively, insert the factor 1/Re into the Stokes projector definition so the cross terms cancel exactly. Either fix is local and preserves the O(h^{min{l,m}} + τ) rate.
issues.overall_effect: The step producing the differential inequality used for the discrete Gronwall estimate is not established as displayed. The omitted cross term is O(‖∇ψ_u‖ ‖∇ξ_u‖) and can be absorbed by Young's inequality without changing the convergence rate, but the error equation as written is missing it.
issues.title: Error equation in the convergence proof omits a projection-pressure cross term
issues.why_classification: The missing term has the same structure as other projection-error cross terms already estimated in the proof and is absorbed by a routine Young's inequality step (or by a one-line change to the projector definition). All claims and rates survive without new arguments.
